signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.26, holding above its SMA20 and SMA50 at 157.65 and 157.71 while capped below the SMA200 at 158.54. The SOFR-TONA carry spread of +264bp structurally favors USD longs, with Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% providing a 275bp policy gap. However, the options market exhibits acute downside hedging demand, with 25d risk reversals printing at -1.80 alongside a negative vol risk premium of -1.8% as ATM IV runs at 7.9% against HV30 of 9.7%. This heavy put skew signals aggressive hedging against sudden sharp pullbacks, while 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered BoJ verbal warnings. JPY CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short -30,379 contracts at the 90th percentile of its 52-week range, leaving the carry trade historically crowded. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; elevated carry return sustains the trend while below-normal options vol requires downside vigilance. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI prints materially below forecast, triggering a rapid options-led unwind through the 157.65 moving-average support.

signals.title: NOK/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Bias
signals.text: NOK leads the G10 strength scorecard with a 1-week average gain of +0.729% across 2 pairs, while JPY anchors the bottom with a 1-week average decline of -0.313% across 7 pairs. This produces a bilateral divergence spread of 1.042%, triggering the G10 bilateral theme threshold. The outperformance is fundamentally anchored by monetary divergence, as Norges Bank holds a restrictive real policy rate of +1.82% at 4.5% against the BoJ's negative real rate of -2.25% at 1.25%. Geopolitical supply frictions reflected in elevated energy prices continue to bolster the petroleum-linked Krone while penalizing Japan's terms of trade. Furthermore, retail positioning on NOK/JPY sits at an extreme 93% short, presenting contrarian fuel for extension. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/JPY; policy rate divergence and retail short imbalance support outperformance. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting 5 Nov. Risk: Broad equity market downturn compresses high-beta cross carry, prompting swift JPY short covering.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short vs Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1212, depressed below its descending SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200 cluster at 1.1327, 1.1492, and 1.1594. CFTC data reveals Leveraged Funds net short EUR by -84,775 contracts, resting at the 4th percentile of its 52-week distribution with a z-score of -1.64, signaling an oversold, crowded short base. In the options space, 1-month ATM IV of 6.5% trades 2.2 points above HV30 of 4.3%, indicating an elevated vol risk premium as traders pay up for tail protection into key event risk. The fundamental backdrop remains anchored by SOFR-€STR carry of +143bp in favor of USD, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65%. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; strong structural USD carry dominance limits topside momentum, though crowded positioning warns against chasing breakdowns. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US headline inflation undershoots consensus, inducing an aggressive short-covering squeeze toward the SMA20 resistance at 1.1327.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Rhetoric vs OIS Rate Spread
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3270, struggling below its SMA20 of 1.3269, SMA50 of 1.3431, and SMA200 of 1.3437. Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill struck a cautious tone today, expressing scepticism regarding market expectations for four rate hikes over the coming year. This pushback against hawkish terminal pricing arrives while the cross-market rates backdrop already heavily favors the greenback, with US 5Y yields up 24bp over the past 20 sessions led by real yields adding 33bp according to FRED data. The SOFR-SONIA spread offers a modest +14bp USD carry advantage, while the policy rate differential shows Fed at 4.00% vs BoE at 3.75%. Options skew remains defensive with GBP/USD 25d risk reversals at -0.77, reflecting ongoing put preference. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; central bank rate pushback combined with US real yield strength caps topside progress. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: UK growth or inflation prints re-accelerate sharply, forcing BoE hawks to reassert multi-hike guidance.
evidence: BoE MPC Pill headline: sceptical on 4 hikes
